meta_title: KTB Health: clinical documentation for medical conversations
meta_description: KTB Health is a clinical documentation platform: it listens to the consultation, transcribes it, structures the anamnesis with evidence citations and hands the physician a draft to review and sign. The physician decides; KTB Health records.
hero_title: A clinical record, ready for review.
hero_subtitle: A clinical documentation platform: it listens to the consultation, transcribes it, structures the anamnesis with evidence citations and hands the physician a draft to review. In person, teleconsultation or phone, without changing the physician’s workflow.
problem_body: The physician sees the patient. Who documents? A study of 57 physicians found that only 27% of the office day goes to the patient, while almost half goes to the EHR and desk work.
problem_stat1_label: of the office day with the patient
problem_stat2_label: on the EHR and desk work
problem_stat3_label: of documentation for every hour with the patient, plus 1–2 hours each night
problem_source: Source: Sinsky C. et al. Allocation of Physician Time in Ambulatory Practice. Annals of Internal Medicine, 2016;165(11):753-760. Direct observation of 57 physicians in 4 specialties, USA; night hours from diaries of 21 of them.
steps_subtitle: From the conversation to a signed record, in four steps.
step1_body: The ambient scribe listens to the consultation, always after the patient’s explicit consent.
step2_body: The audio is stored and transcribed in Brazilian Portuguese.
step3_body: It drafts the anamnesis with evidence citations. Hypotheses and treatment stay with the physician.
step4_body: The physician reviews, edits and approves. Nothing enters the record without a signature.
principle1_body: Never issues a diagnosis, never decides treatment, never suggests what the physician should think, never replaces clinical judgment. Human-in-the-loop is not a feature: it is the whole product.
principle2_body: The final record always belongs to the physician, who reviews, edits and approves the draft. Nothing enters the medical record without a signature.
principle3_title: Clinical data stays where it belongs
principle3_body: Capture only after explicit consent, audio under the physician’s control, the option to run fully in your own environment (on-premise), and synthetic data in demos and tests. LGPD by architecture, not by disclaimer.
principle4_body: In person, teleconsultation or phone. No lock-in and no change to the physician’s workflow.
who_body: Physicians running teleconsultations or in-person visits who want their time back. We start with telemedicine; in-person care is core to the vision. Built for the Brazilian healthcare context first, with B2C self-serve for individual doctors.
vision_body: Why now: ambient documentation is the next frontier of digital health, screen time already beats time with the patient, and whoever gets there first with trust defines the category. What comes next: our own consultation channel, so KTB becomes the environment and not just the capture, and patient history, with context across consultations.
